findings.title: Test won't compile below API level 9: missing SEASTAR_API_LEVEL guard on put(std::span)…
findings.claim: The new test overrides put(std::span<…>) without #if SEASTAR_API_LEVEL >= 9 like every other sink in the tree (e.g. tests/unit/loopback_socket.hh:144), so rpc_test breaks at the lower levels CMake still offers, which matters for the backport the PR asks for.

findings.title: Test never exercises the drain half of the fix (stream_close queue wait)
findings.claim: sink_impl::close() waits for the end-of-stream send before calling close_sink(), so the queue is always empty when stream_close() runs; the test would stay green if the std::exchange(_outgoing_queue_ready…) wait at src/rpc/rpc.cc:562-570 were reverted.

findings.title: Test never asserts the refusal; accepts both success and closed_error
findings.claim: tests/unit/rpc_test.cc:2016-2019 accepts both success and closed_error outcomes; the test fails only if the batch-flush poller later writes, so a regression that accepts the frame but defers or drops it would pass.

findings.title: "Let the batch flush poller run" comment is wrong; yield() doesn't poll for I/O
findings.claim: yield() queues a task and does not poll for I/O (include/seastar/util/later.hh:41-44), so the loop doesn't run the poller; on base, detection depends on later .get() calls happening to poll, otherwise on the destructor assert.

findings.title: Test failures hang or abort instead of reporting cleanly
findings.claim: close_entered_cv.wait at :2011 has no timeout; if BOOST_REQUIRE_EQUAL at :2000 fails, the sink is dropped unclosed and ~sink_impl's SEASTAR_ASSERT aborts the process; if the hook throws anything other than closed_error, release_close is never set; existing stream tests avoid this with deferred_close(sink).

findings.title: Cross-shard data race in hook_capturing_compressor_factory::negotiate
findings.claim: negotiate (:1957) pushes into one shard-0 std::vector; with -c 2, loopback round-robin accepts the parent connection on shard 0 and the stream connection on shard 1, so both server-side negotiations write to it unsynchronized; recording only when !is_server fixes it since server hooks are never used.

findings.title: New comment misstates the cause of _outgoing_queue_ready becoming exceptional
findings.claim: src/rpc/rpc.cc:566-567 says _outgoing_queue_ready "is exceptional if an entry failed," but a failed send_entry calls abort() and then p->done.set_value() (:333-338); the future only becomes exceptional through stop_send_loop while _negotiated is still pending. The code itself is harmless.

findings.title: Docs wrongly claim reading a source until it throws always closes it
findings.claim: include/seastar/rpc/rpc_types.hh:384-389 and doc/rpc-streaming.md:110-112 say reading a source until it throws closes it, but an unmarshall exception in source_impl::operator() (rpc_impl.hh:948) propagates without close_source(); an application that stops reading after never triggers stream_close(), which is the leak these docs warn about.

findings.title: Docs overstate that the connection is shut down "only once" both halves are closed
findings.claim: doc/rpc-streaming.md:115 says the connection is shut down only once both halves are closed, but it is also shut down on peer EOF, on error, and through abort_all_streams.

findings.title: Docs understate the consequence of dropping an unclosed sink
findings.claim: doc/rpc-streaming.md:109 says "Dropping an unclosed sink is an error," but it is an always-on SEASTAR_ASSERT that aborts the process.

findings.title: New wait in stream_close() claimed to be a regression/unbounded
findings.claim: A claim that the new wait in stream_close() is a problem; rejected because it is bounded the same way base write_buf.close() was, so it is not a regression.

findings.title: Close-vs-shutdown race claimed as a problem
findings.claim: A claim about a close-vs-shutdown race; rejected because it is bounded the same way base write_buf.close() was, so it is not a regression.

findings.title: Parent client in the PR body claimed to have an unfixed write-after-close path
findings.claim: A claim that the parent client has an unfixed write-after-close path, citing a 141-byte frame; rejected because the parent has no unfixed path and the frame is ordinary in-flight state.

findings.title: error() callers claimed able to reach send() on a closing stream connection
findings.claim: A claim about error() callers versus the new _stream_closing flag; rejected because none of the callers can reach send() on a closing stream connection.
